description: A public/external function (often an underscore-prefixed 'internal-style' helper accidentally left public) lets any caller mutate per-user/global index/array bookkeeping for an ARBITRARY address with no access control, corrupting enumeration or desyncing index<->array invariants so a later legitimate operation reverts or mis-accounts. Anchored on Phi 2024-08 H-05 (public `_addCredIdPerAddress`/`_removeCredIdPerAddress` corrupt any holder's cred-list -> sell-DoS / bookkeeping corruption).

poc_level_descriptors.L3A: show the index/array mutator is public/external with no auth and takes an arbitrary target address
poc_level_descriptors.L3B: as an unrelated attacker, call it for a victim address; assert the index<->array bookkeeping is desynced / array bloated (read the storage)
poc_level_descriptors.L3C: assert a later legitimate op for the victim reverts (IndexOutofBounds/WrongCredId-style) or mis-accounts, and that it scales to many/all holders (permanent without privileged repair)

high_severity_rationale: High requires proving the corruption causes a downstream revert/mis-accounting for legitimate users AND affects many/all holders (current and upcoming) without self-recovery. Medium is proven by the public unguarded mutator + arbitrary-address corruption alone. This is access-control / unauthorized state mutation (P88 keeps it via concrete unauthorized_execution); per the P90 maximal-consequence check, the all-holders + permanent-corruption angle should be tested before settling on Medium (cf. H-05 under-rated Medium vs awarded High).
negative_control_template: Restrict the mutator: make it internal (remove `public`/`external`) or add a guard so only the contract's own buy/sell path can call it. Assert an external attacker call reverts and the victim's index<->array bookkeeping + later operations are unaffected.
